name: Labradford
label: Kranky
lede: Two Richmond friends named their band after a college basketball player, mailed out a 7-inch so out of step that two men at a Chicago distributor started Kranky just to release their album, then drifted to a stop without ever breaking up.

eras.title: A label built for one record
eras.text: Labradford began in Richmond, Virginia as a duo: Mark Nelson on guitar, tapes and voice, Carter Brown on analog synths and organ. Their slow, dark drone rock sounded like nothing around them, and it reached exactly the right desk in Chicago.

years.h: Mark Nelson and Carter Brown start Labradford in Richmond
years.p: Guitarist Mark Nelson and keyboardist Carter Brown, who had studied organ in Richmond for two years, form a duo built on old analog synths and treated guitar.

years.h: Labradford is named after a Louisville basketball player
years.p: Bassist Robert Donne told the Weedbus fanzine the name comes from LaBradford Smith, a Louisville basketball player who went on to the NBA's Washington Bullets.

years.h: Labradford's debut 7-inch, Everlast, on Retro 8
years.p: The first single comes out on the small Retro 8 label, which also puts a Labradford track on its Repugnating the Wombat compilation.

q: What they were doing was so uncommercial, so unique, and so compelling
years.src: Bandcamp Daily: Kranky at 25 · Chicago Reader: Kranky and Proud of It · Wikipedia: Kranky
years.h: Joel Leoschke and Bruce Adams start Kranky to release Labradford
years.p: Labradford's 7-inch lands on Leoschke's desk at the Chicago distributor Cargo. He and Cargo colleague Bruce Adams, a former Touch and Go publicist, found Kranky to put out the band's album.
years.xp:
Leoschke had spent five years as Cargo's domestic buyer and knew how new labels failed. They nearly called it Curmudgeon, but Leoschke said it had too many syllables.

Three decades on the roster runs from [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]] to [[Deerhunter|4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b]], and Labradford is still krank 001.

years.src: Wikipedia: Prazision LP · John Peel Wiki
years.h: Prazision LP · krank 001
years.p: Recorded at McKinley Hall and the Belt Trade Center in Richmond, with Carter Brown on Memorymoog, Polymoog and a Roland vocoder. [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] had played the debut single that year and kept the album in his collection.

eras.title: Losing the words
eras.text: With bassist Robert Donne, an old Richmond friend from the hard rock band Breadwinner, Labradford started writing as a trio and let the vocals slip away. Strings, chains and live percussion crept in, and Stars of the Lid and Stereolab became company.

q: they just asked me to join and have a go at playing with them
years.h: Robert Donne joins Labradford after Prazision LP
years.p: Donne had known Carter Brown for about ten years and played in Breadwinner. After the debut, Brown and Mark Nelson simply invited him in.
years.xp: From then on, Donne said, the three wrote songs together instead of playing the duo's older material.

years.h: Labradford records its first John Peel session
years.p: Starcity, Accelerating on a Smoother Road, Balanced on Its Own Flame and Comfort air on [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s BBC Radio 1 show on November 19. The band also lands on Virgin's Ambient 4: Isolationism compilation.

years.h: A Stable Reference: Robert Donne arrives, the vocals leave
years.p: Recorded at American University in Washington, D.C. AllMusic's Ned Raggett notes that lyrics disappear from nearly every track.

years.h: Labradford tours with Stereolab and Tortoise
years.p: Labradford supports [[Stereolab|f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6]] and [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] in 1995, after earlier dates opening for Archers of Loaf. Merge Records also releases the Julius 7-inch.

years.h: Labradford: violin, sequencers and chains played live
years.p: The self-titled third album adds strings arranged by classical violinist Chris Johnston. Robert Donne says the chains scraping on Phantom Channel Crossing were all played live.
years.xp: A second Peel session followed in May 1996. That year Labradford also split the Kahanek Incident, Vol. 3 12-inch with Austin's [[Stars of the Lid|a1154343-1ea1-4007-97d3-2382482a90cd]] on Trance Syndicate, and put out Scenic Recovery on Stereolab's Duophonic label.

years.h: Mi Media Naranja: Fender Rhodes, slide guitar and strings
years.p: Labradford's fourth Kranky album, its title a Spanish idiom for one's other half. Brainwashed notes the string section, Rhodes and slide guitar that now fill out the sound.

eras.title: Festival of Drifting
eras.text: Labradford became curators as much as a band, putting their name on London festivals alongside Brian Eno's music and Tony Conrad. By the end the three lived in different cities, made one last record with Steve Albini, and quietly stopped.

years.h: Labradford's first Festival of Drifting takes over London's South Bank
years.p: Ten days at the Royal Festival Hall, Queen Elizabeth Hall and Purcell Room, with Brian Eno's Music for Airports, John Martyn, Tony Conrad, Pan Sonic and Michael Gira.
years.xp: Presented by Foundation, the BBC and Blast First, Labradford's UK label, the festival ran to October 3. The bill also had The Durutti Column, Charlemagne Palestine, Bill Nelson and writer Iain Sinclair.

years.h: Mark Nelson's Pan American releases its debut on Kranky
years.p: Nelson's solo project [[Pan American|eeef9e6a-460b-49ca-840f-b55481b47297]], started in 1997 for music too electronic for Labradford, becomes one of Kranky's longest-running names.

years.src: Cerysmatic Factory: Festival of Drifting 1999 · Wikipedia · Brainwashed
years.h: The second Festival of Drifting moves into a London church
years.p: Four nights at Union Chapel in Islington, a working church, with spin-off shows in Sheffield and Edinburgh. Wikipedia lists [[Sigur Rós|f6f2326f-6b25-4170-b89d-e235b25508e8]], [[Matmos|46e8a8ee-d2cd-4165-9725-02f72d0027a9]], Pole and [[Papa M|6edbe0fb-734e-4b1d-9c64-73ebb04853e1]] among the series' acts.

years.h: E Luxo So: every song title is a list of credits
years.p: Recorded at Sound of Music in Richmond, with strings and dulcimer by Peter Neff. Its six tracks are named after the players and engineers on them.
years.xp: NME gave it 8 out of 10; Pitchfork gave it 5.3. Released by Blast First in the UK and Kranky in the US.

yt: Live at Lounge Ax, Chicago, September 16, 1999
years.h: Labradford tours North America with Godspeed You! Black Emperor
years.p: By now the three live in Richmond, Washington, D.C. and Chicago. Labradford crosses North America with [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]].

years.h: Labradford plays Fixed::Context straight through at Schubas
years.p: The Chicago Reader previews a Schubas show where Labradford will play the new album's four pieces in order. By now Brown has swapped synths for piano and organ, and Nelson has stopped singing.

years.h: Fixed::Context: four pieces with Steve Albini, then silence
years.p: Recorded in July 2000 at Electrical Audio in Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], on Blast First and Kranky. The Guardian heard Duane Eddy playing the Twin Peaks theme.
years.xp: No breakup was ever announced, and Labradford has released nothing since. Wikipedia notes that Coil were friends who had planned to collaborate with the band.

eras.title: Never broke up, never came back
eras.text: Labradford has never officially disbanded. Two-thirds of the band reunited under a new name, and its music turned up somewhere nobody expected: a prestige TV drama about a fictional pope.

years.h: Mark Nelson and Robert Donne return as Anjou
years.p: Two Labradford members and Pan American drummer [[Steven Hess|f6e3c48b-fe51-42b0-b002-9d77da680442]] release Anjou on Kranky after four years' work. A second album, Epithymía, follows in 2017.
years.xp: In the Labradford silence Donne had made Aix Em Klemm with [[Stars of the Lid|a1154343-1ea1-4007-97d3-2382482a90cd]]'s [[Adam Wiltzie|fa7d8199-ba6a-448c-b25a-a615261fe6e6]], recorded as Cristal, played with Spokane and toured with [[Gregor Samsa|3c651564-eb88-48e0-a862-d6db17e8464a]]. He also played bass on Pan American's 2013 album.

years.h: A Labradford track scores Paolo Sorrentino's The Young Pope
years.p: By Chris Johnston, Craig Markva, Jamie Evans, from E Luxo So, plays across several episodes of the HBO series, fifteen years after the band's last release.
